title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page belongs to the 1976 IHES lecture on the divided-power (pd) de Rham complex. The programme is to produce, for a ring k in a topos X, an integral, strictly commutative cochain model, with divided powers, of the cohomology of the topos. It is an integral analogue of Sullivan's rational polynomial forms. The page has five parts.

(1) Top diagrams: independence of choices. Suppose k admits several 'de Rham' k-algebras u: k -> Omega, Omega', Omega''. Grothendieck compares them through common targets N, N', N''. These are presumably tensor products such as Omega ⊗_k Omega', or algebras receiving all of them. This gives a zigzag DR(Omega), DR(Omega'), DR(Omega'') -> DR(N''). If the maps are quasi-isomorphisms, the resulting object (derived global sections / cochain model) is independent of the choice of u up to canonical quasi-isomorphism. This is the standard roof argument for showing a construction is well defined in a derived category.

(2) 'Analogous arguments for f_*(DR_pd(k,u)), f: X -> Y a morphism of topoi.' The same argument gives a well-defined relative version: a pd commutative dg model of Rf_* k.

(3) Definition: 'condition de De Rham' on a ring k of the topos. One requires a k-algebra u: k -> Omega such that the pd de Rham complex DR_pd(k,u) is a resolution of k by objects acyclic for the relevant functors (a pd Poincare lemma plus acyclicity). If k satisfies it, so does every k-algebra, by base change. So the best case is that Z_X satisfies it. Grothendieck says this holds for:
- (a) the topos of simplicial sets, Delta^. Here Omega is presumably the pd-polynomial forms on standard simplices. These satisfy an integral pd Poincare lemma and the extension property that makes Sullivan's construction work.
- (b) the topos of a paracompact topological space, via some fine/soft-type resolution.
He then asks whether it holds for the topos of cosimplicial objects (Delta°^) or for some class of algebras (complete intersections?). The answer is an emphatic 'Non' (underlined three times).

(4) Pd envelope / resolution of an algebra. Take A^{**} in DR_pd^{**}(X), a bigraded pd dg algebra in positive degrees, with A^{00} = k satisfying the condition, and choose u: k -> Omega. Define
  Ā^{**} = DR_pd(A^{**}) := DR_pd^{**}(k,u) ⊗_{k{T}} A^{**},
where k{T} is the universal (free pd-polynomial) de Rham algebra. The augmentation k{T} -> DR_pd(k,u) is a quasi-isomorphism, and universally so. Hence the canonical map A^{**} -> Ā^{**} is a quasi-isomorphism. Ā is an 'envelope' (the last word) whose components are presumably acyclic. This is a functorial replacement of a pd commutative dg algebra by an acyclic one, for computing derived global sections or pushforwards inside pd-commutative algebras.

(5) Purpose. The aim is to show that RΓ(X,k), and Rf_*, carry a canonical structure of strictly commutative pd dg algebra, well defined up to quasi-isomorphism and functorial in the topos. It is an integral substitute for Sullivan's A_PL and for Thom–Whitney/Navarro-Aznar style constructions.
errors: The transcription garbles most words, so the precise statement of the 'condition de De Rham' is not legible. The reconstruction (acyclic resolution via DR_pd(k,u)) is inferred from context.

Claim (b) for paracompact spaces is stated without proof. It is not obvious which integral sheaf of pd algebras Omega with acyclic de Rham components would work for Z. Soft sheaves of continuous functions are not Z-algebras with a Poincare lemma over Z. This may be a gap or may depend on a construction from earlier pages.

Strict commutativity with divided powers cannot capture Steenrod operations integrally or mod p (cf. later results on E∞ cochains). So any such model can only preserve the pd-commutative structure, not the full homotopy type. The page does not address this limitation, though it may be discussed elsewhere in the lecture.

ideas.what: Integral pd-polynomial de Rham forms on simplices as a strictly commutative cochain model of the cohomology of simplicial sets
ideas.modern_name: Divided-power polynomial de Rham forms; integral analogue of Sullivan's A_PL (cf. Cartan's 1976 'Théories cohomologiques', Cenkl–Porter, Karoubi's integral de Rham)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Sullivan (rational, 1977); integral/pd variants by H. Cartan (1976), Cenkl–Porter (late 1970s/80s), Karoubi (1990s)

ideas.what: 'Condition de De Rham' on a ring of a topos: existence of u: k -> Omega with DR_pd(k,u) an acyclic resolution; stable under base change; verified for Z in Delta^ and in paracompact spaces; fails for another topos/class
ideas.modern_name: Existence of a strictly commutative (pd) cochain model / sheaf of commutative dg algebras resolving the constant sheaf, for a general topos
ideas.usually_credited_to: Not standard as such. Related ideas appear in Navarro Aznar (Thom–Whitney cochains on sites/diagrams, 1987).

ideas.what: Independence of the choice of Omega via zigzags through common targets N, and relative version f_* for morphisms of topoi
ideas.modern_name: Well-definedness of a derived pushforward in pd-cdga's up to quasi-isomorphism

ideas.what: Replacement A -> DR_pd(k,u) ⊗_{k{T}} A, a quasi-isomorphism by universality of k{T} -> DR_pd(k,u), giving an acyclic 'envelope' of a bigraded pd algebra
ideas.modern_name: Functorial acyclic (Thom–Whitney/Godement-type) resolution of commutative dg algebras by base change along a universal quasi-isomorphism
ideas.usually_credited_to: Navarro Aznar 1987 (Thom–Whitney); Hinich–Schechtman for commutative structures on cochains

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates a general axiomatic 'de Rham condition' for rings in an arbitrary topos. It would guarantee a strictly commutative pd cochain model of RΓ and Rf_*. He checks it for simplicial sets and paracompact spaces and finds a negative case. A general theory of which topoi admit integral pd-commutative cochain models (versus only E∞ ones) does not appear to have been developed in this form.
missed.quote: Conditions de DeRham sur Anneau k : la condition d'existence d'un u : k → Ω tel que.... Dans le plus beau, c'est que Z_X y satisfasse !
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This bears on integral homotopy theory and on the relation between E∞ cochains and strictly commutative pd models: when the pd structure suffices and where the obstructions lie. It also anticipates derived/pd de Rham methods in topos-theoretic generality.

missed.claim: Early (1976) linking of crystalline-style divided-power de Rham complexes with Sullivan-type models of the homotopy theory of simplicial sets and topological spaces, inside topos theory.
missed.quote: C'est vrai pour a) le topos SS Δ̂ b) le topos défini par un espace topologique paracompact.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This prefigures integral and p-adic approaches to homotopy types via pd algebras (Mandell-style questions, derived de Rham). The Grothendieck lecture is rarely cited in that literature.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a sketch, but it documents Grothendieck working on integral pd-commutative cochain models in topos-theoretic generality in 1976. He states a 'de Rham condition', verifies it for simplicial sets and paracompact spaces, and gives a negative answer for another case. The underlying ideas parallel known work (Sullivan, Cartan, Navarro Aznar), so the novelty is moderate rather than striking.
transcription_corrections: 'Arguments analogues pour f_*(DR^{**}_{pd}(k,u)), où f: X → Y morphisme de topos' — the image shows (k,u), not (h,u).
'Conditions de DeRham sur Anneau k' is likely 'Condition de De Rham sur Anneau k'.
'Si k satisfait condition de De Rham, de même tout k-algèbre' — plausible reading of the garbled line.
'DR^{**}_{pd}(h)' in the definition of Ā should read 'DR^{**}_{pd}(k,u) ⊗_{k{T}} A^{**}' (with a struck-out symbol).
'(qui est un quasi-iso universel)' — 'universel' is underlined.
The final line ends with 'Enveloppe' written over a struck-out word; the dagger symbols are bars (Ā^{**}).
